I'll start by reading the two guide documents, then survey the API app structure to compare against them.

[package]
name = "meno-api"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
rust-version.workspace = true
license.workspace = true
description = "Meno HTTP API and background worker."

# Two binaries from one crate (Step 3.6): the web server and the job worker. Same
# image, same dependencies, different entry point — see src/main.rs and src/worker.rs.
[[bin]]
name = "meno-api"
path = "src/main.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "meno-worker"
path = "src/worker.rs"

[lib]
name = "meno_api"
path = "src/lib.rs"

# Declared incrementally: this manifest lists what the modules that exist *today* need
# (`config`, `infrastructure/*`, `middleware`, `types` and `modules/auth`). The plan's
# remaining adapter — apalis for §6's job queue — is added when `jobs/` lands to use it,
# because an unused dependency is a build-time cost nobody chose.
[features]
# Test doubles, made reachable from outside the crate.
#
# Rust's integration tests live in `tests/` and link `meno_api` as an *external*
# dependency, where `#[cfg(test)]` is false — so an in-memory repository gated that way
# does not exist as far as they are concerned. This feature is the alternative to
# ungating unconditionally: `cargo test` turns it on automatically for the test targets,
# while a production build compiles none of the doubles.
#
# Nothing here is reachable from a deployment binary, because a deployment builds with
# `--no-default-features` semantics by simply not asking for this feature.
test-support = []

[dependencies]
meno-core = { workspace = true }

anyhow = { workspace = true }
# `argon2` is the password KDF (plan S3.2): hashing and verifying, both on
# `spawn_blocking` because a single verification costs ~50ms of deliberate work.
argon2 = { workspace = true }
async-trait = { workspace = true }
axum = { workspace = true }
# `/metrics` (§7.5): the Prometheus recorder plus the axum layer and endpoint.
axum-prometheus = { workspace = true }
bytes = { workspace = true }
dashmap = { workspace = true }
# `http-body-util` is what `BodyExt::collect` comes from. The idempotency middleware has
# to buffer a response body to cache it (§4.5: the replay must carry the body *and* its
# `Content-Type`), and axum's `Body` implements `http_body::Body`, not the concrete
# buffering traits — so this is a genuine runtime dependency, not a test convenience.
http-body-util = { workspace = true }
# `config` is required by §4.6 ("replace `env::var` + `Context` chains with a typed,
# layered config ... with a single aggregated error"). It is declared in the workspace
# manifest and used by `config.rs` via the `ConfigSource` trait, which keeps the
# parsing testable without mutating the process environment.
config = { workspace = true }
dotenvy = { workspace = true }
fred = { workspace = true }
# `futures_util` splits the axum WebSocket into its sink and stream halves for the
# `/ws` read/write/heartbeat loop (`routes::ws`), which is three tasks over one socket.
futures-util = { workspace = true }
# `hex` renders the SHA-256 digest a refresh token is stored as; `sha2` computes it. A
# refresh token is never stored verbatim, so a database dump holds nothing replayable.
hex = { workspace = true }
jsonwebtoken = { workspace = true }
livekit-api = { workspace = true }
livekit-protocol = { workspace = true }

CREATE FUNCTION update_user_broadcast_count() RETURNS TRIGGER AS
$$
BEGIN
    IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN
        IF NEW.deleted_at IS NULL THEN
            UPDATE public.users SET broadcasts = broadcasts + 1 WHERE id = NEW.creator_id;
        END IF;

    ELSIF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN
        IF OLD.deleted_at IS NULL AND NEW.deleted_at IS NOT NULL THEN
            UPDATE public.users SET broadcasts = broadcasts - 1 WHERE id = OLD.creator_id;
        ELSIF OLD.deleted_at IS NOT NULL AND NEW.deleted_at IS NULL THEN
            UPDATE public.users SET broadcasts = broadcasts + 1 WHERE id = NEW.creator_id;
        ELSIF OLD.creator_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.creator_id THEN
            UPDATE public.users SET broadcasts = broadcasts - 1 WHERE id = OLD.creator_id;
            UPDATE public.users SET broadcasts = broadcasts + 1 WHERE id = NEW.creator_id;
        END IF;

    ELSIF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN
        IF OLD.deleted_at IS NULL THEN
            UPDATE public.users SET broadcasts = broadcasts - 1 WHERE id = OLD.creator_id;
        END IF;
    END IF;

    RETURN NULL;
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

    AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF deleted_at, creator_id OR DELETE ON public.broadcasts

======== 0017_broadcast_liveness.sql
-- Two things a broadcast needs and the schema could not express before:
--
-- 1. **One account, one broadcast on air.** Nothing stopped a creator from having
--    several rows in `active` at once — two editor sessions, a retry, or a client
--    that lost the answer to its own go-live all produced a second live broadcast.
--    A partial unique index is the only place that can be true of every writer,
--    including two replicas racing the same request.
--
-- 2. **When a broadcast first met an end condition.** The reaper ends a broadcast
--    nobody is in, or whose host has not come back, only after a grace period; the
--    clock has to survive a restart of the process that started it, so it lives here
--    rather than in a job's memory.

-- Repair first: a single creator with more than one live row makes the unique index
-- impossible to build, and leaving the extra rows live is what the index exists to
-- stop. The newest row (by publish time) per creator stays on air; the rest are
-- closed as forced ends, which is an honest description of what happened to them.
UPDATE public.broadcasts AS b
SET status     = 'inactive',
    end_time   = COALESCE(b.end_time, now()),
    end_reason = COALESCE(b.end_reason, 'admin_forced'),
    updated_at = now()
WHERE b.status = 'active'
  AND b.deleted_at IS NULL
  AND b.id NOT IN (
      SELECT DISTINCT ON (live.creator_id) live.id
      FROM public.broadcasts AS live
      WHERE live.status = 'active'
        AND live.deleted_at IS NULL
      ORDER BY live.creator_id, live.published_at DESC NULLS LAST, live.created_at DESC, live.id
  );

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_broadcasts_one_live_per_creator
    ON public.broadcasts (creator_id)
    WHERE status = 'active' AND deleted_at IS NULL;

-- Null while the broadcast is in a healthy state; set to the moment it first became
-- abandonable (nobody in the room, or no host and no cohost) and cleared when somebody
-- comes back. The reaper compares it against now() rather than counting down in memory.
ALTER TABLE public.broadcasts
    ADD COLUMN abandoned_since TIMESTAMPTZ(3);

COMMENT ON COLUMN public.broadcasts.abandoned_since IS
    'When the broadcast first had nobody in its room, or no host and no cohost. Cleared when that stops being true.';

//! `GET /ws` — upgrading an authenticated socket and running its lifetime.
//!
//! # Why the token travels in the query string
//!
//! A browser cannot set an `Authorization` header on a WebSocket handshake, so the
//! access token arrives as `?token=` — the shape [`WsQuery`] documents: a missing
//! parameter fails to deserialise, so an unauthenticated handshake is refused before
//! a socket exists. That puts authentication *inside* this handler rather than behind
//! [`crate::middleware::auth::auth_middleware`], but it does not duplicate the gate:
//! both surfaces call [`AuthState::authenticate`], the one method that owns
//! verify-then-blocklist. A rule that lives in two places is a rule that eventually
//! applies to only one of them.
//!
//! # What the pre-upgrade gate enforces, in order
//!
//! 1. A non-empty token ([`required_token`]).
//! 2. Signature, expiry and revocation (`AuthState::authenticate`).
//! 3. A verified email address — `master`'s gate, kept: everything downstream of the
//!    socket (chat, presence) assumes the address was confirmed.
//! 4. A reconnect-rate limit ([`check_reconnect_rate`]), **fail closed** (§4.4): a
//!    limiter whose Redis is down must not become an unthrottled reconnect storm.
//! 5. The per-user connection cap, so an over-limit caller gets a clean 429 rather
//!    than a socket that opens and immediately closes.
//!
//! Each step short-circuits with the §4.2 error envelope, so a refused handshake
//! reads exactly like a refused HTTP request.
//!
//! # What runs on a connection, and what deliberately does not
//!
//! Wired here: presence, offline-buffer replay, the server-side heartbeat (pings every
//! [`HeartbeatConfig::ping_interval_secs`], a pong deadline that closes the socket),
//! frame dispatch through [`WsEvent::is_client_to_server`], and the cleanup that
//! unregisters the socket and clears presence.
//!
//! Wired since the chat module landed: the four chat frames are parsed, validated and
//! dispatched into [`crate::modules::chat::service`] by [`handle_chat_frame`], and a
//! refusal comes back as the socket code the client can act on.
//!

//! `modules::broadcast` and `jobs/`; those events are answered with an honest "not
//! available yet" connection error, and the room bookkeeping attaches to

The module exists and is real: 14 HTTP endpoints, LiveKit token/room integration, a cross-replica WS delivery layer, an abandonment reaper, and a schema that already carries most of v2's columns. # Broadcast module — spec vs implementation review

**Verdict in one line:** the core is built and is arguably better layered than the docs ask for, but three structural decisions diverge from the spec — transport (HTTP instead of WS for end/leave), the grace-period mechanism (DB reaper instead of Redis tiered grace), and auth scope (everything private) — and the entire v2 feature set below §7 is unbuilt, even though its tables and enum variants are already in the schema.

The implementation follows v2's *naming* (`participants`, `participantJoined`, no `livekitUrl`) but v1's *transport*. Where the two docs disagree, that's the rule it applied.

## 2. Where it has veered off

### Significant — protocol or semantics

1. **End/leave are HTTP; the socket knows nothing about them.** [`WsEvent`](apps/api/src/infrastructure/ws/model.rs#L30) has no `EndBroadcast` or `LeaveBroadcast` variant, so a client following §3.5/§10.2 sends `{"event":"endBroadcast"}` and gets **`malformed WS frame`** in the log and *no reply* — not even the "unsupported" error other events return. This defeats the docs' stated principle ("the server cleans up on disconnect, not on explicit FE action"): a listener who force-kills the app keeps an open `left_at IS NULL` roster row forever, and the live count never falls. `routes/ws.rs` says so itself: *"Still not wired … room join/leave and the host grace period."*

2. **The host grace period was replaced, not ported.** Docs: tiered 120/90/60/30s in Redis, triggered by the host's *socket* dropping, emitting `hostDisconnected { gracePeriodSecs, disconnectCount }` and `hostReconnected`. Implementation: a flat **10 minutes**, driven by polling **LiveKit participant lists** every 60s, persisted in `broadcasts.abandoned_since`. Redis keys `host_grace`, `grace_started`, `disconnect_count` and `GracePeriodConfig` exist and are **only referenced by their own tests**; `WsPayload::host_disconnected/host_reconnected` are built but never emitted in production code. Side effect: `state: "reconnecting"` now means "LiveKit reports nobody in the room", not "the host's socket blipped" — different failure modes, different client UI.

3. **Everything is authenticated.** §5.1 and the v2 endpoint table mark `GET /broadcasts`, `/:id`, `/participants`, `/now-live`, `/recently-live` as public (some `OptionalAuth`). Here [`routes/broadcasts.rs`](apps/api/src/routes/broadcasts.rs) applies `auth_middleware` to the whole nest. Consequence: `ParticipantRole::None` is unreachable, and `viewer_role` can never be `NONE`, which is exactly the "am I the host?" ambiguity v2 §6 exists to remove.

4. **`newBroadcast` only reaches the creator's own devices.** Docs: fan out to subscribers via the follow graph (and create in-app notifications). Here it's `&[actor.id]`, with a non-spec `homeInvalidated` broadcast to everyone instead. The `subscribers` module exists, so the follow graph is available — the module just doesn't read it.

5. **`published_at` was repurposed.** It's written by `mark_live` as "when it went live", and `duration_seconds` is computed from it. v2 defines `published_at` as *recording published* time (`has_recording` filter, publish endpoint, idempotent republish). Those two meanings cannot coexist on one column; the recording/publish work will need a rename or a new column.

6. **Cohosts skip the invitation flow.** Direct insert by the creator, limit **3** (`MAX_COHOSTS`), removal optional-evict. v2 §8.6 wants invite → accept/decline (1 cohost). The `cohost_invitations` table **and** `cohostInvitation`/`cohostAccepted`/`cohostDeclined`/`cohostDemotion` payload builders already exist and are unused.

7. **Live counts come from the roster table only.** `live_participant_count` is a `COUNT(*) … WHERE left_at IS NULL` per response; there's no Redis `INCR`/`DECR`, no `mget` batch for lists, and `RedisKey::live_count`/`quota` are dead. `numberOfLiveParticipants` isn't emitted; the count rides on `participantJoined`/`participantLeft` instead. Workable, but it makes every list row a query and loses the tier-3 "exact in-room push".

8. **Token TTL is 15 minutes, not 6 hours**, so refresh is now mandatory rather than rare — yet no response carries `expiresAt`/`tokenExpiresAt`, so the client has to decode the JWT itself to know when. Refresh itself is implemented correctly (role re-read from DB).

9. **End is creator-only; there is no admin path.** Docs say "creator OR admin". Same for the `CANNOT_END` error, which doesn't exist here.

10. **Search is keyset-only.** No `keywords` (the GIN index is unused), no `sort_by`/`order` beyond direction, no `only_subscriptions`, `recently_ended`, `has_recording`, `exclude_creator_id`.

Two schema traps worth naming: `idx_broadcasts_ended_cursor` is built on `status = 'ended'`, but `mark_ended` writes `status = 'inactive'` + `end_time` — that index will never serve the "recently live" query; and `is_draft` is never read or written.

---

## 3. Gaps to fill

**Lifecycle / resilience**
- WS `endBroadcast` + `leaveBroadcast` (with `positionSeconds`), and room join/leave + `hostDisconnected`/`hostReconnected` on socket drop.
- Disconnect-driven roster cleanup, so `left_at` closes when a socket dies.
- `POST /broadcasts/:id/keepalive` (backgrounded apps, non-WS liveness).
- `GET /broadcasts/:id/live-participants` over the media port (already implemented underneath).
- Daily quota: `GET /broadcasts/quota`, enforcement in go-live, deduction on end, mid-broadcast watcher, `DAILY_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` (HTTP + WS), `EndReason::QuotaExceeded` is already modelled.
- `POST /webhooks/livekit` with signature verification and `room_finished`.

**Recording** (modelled in DTO, absent in behaviour): egress start on go-live, `egress_ended` webhook, `recordingReady` emission, `POST /:id/publish`, `GET /:id/recording-url` with presigned S3.

**Discovery / home sections**: `now-live`, `live-for-you`, `recently-live`, `continue-listening`, `listen-later`, `active-session`; keyword search + sort fields; batch Redis live counts.

**Viewer state**: `is_subscribed_to_creator` (subscribers module is right there), real `is_bookmarked` (table + column exist), `time_remaining_seconds` / `last_listened_at` (columns exist, never written), `creator_quota`.

**Social / notifications**: bookmark write endpoints; cohost invite accept/decline; a `notifications` module (table exists at [0012](crates/db/migrations/0012_notifications_schema.sql), no module, and FCM push is built but not called by broadcast — nothing notifies a subscriber that a broadcast started); scheduled-start job (no `apalis` in [Cargo.toml](apps/api/Cargo.toml), and the module docs defer it).

**Docs' own defers**, confirmed accurate: Redis list caching, exceptions for drafts, and the `is_bookmarked` placeholder are all declared honestly in [mod.rs](apps/api/src/modules/broadcast/mod.rs).

---

## 4. Suggested order

1. WS `endBroadcast`/`leaveBroadcast` + disconnect cleanup — until then the "server cleans up" contract is missing and counts drift.
2. Decide `published_at`'s single meaning before any recording work; add `started_at` if you keep "went live".
3. Quota + keepalive (small, mostly Redis, unblocks the Figma go-live and background-audio screens).
4. Open up the public reads with `OptionalAuth` so `viewerRole: NONE` becomes meaningful.
5. Then recording/publish, bookmarks, invites and the home-section presets — in that order, since each depends on the previous (recording → `has_recording` → continue-listening).

I've traced both issues end to end. They are two separate defects that compound — one in the API's transition contract, one in the mobile start chain — which is why fixing either alone won't clear the state you're stuck in.

## 1. Issue 1 — "Continue & Start" always ends in `ALREADY_LIVE`

The editor goes live **twice** in one press.

1. [broadcast_editor_manager.dart:85](apps/mobile/lib/features/broadcast/manager/broadcast_editor_manager.dart#L85) — `startBroadcast` calls `POST /broadcasts/{id}/live` itself.
2. [broadcast_editor_manager.dart:98](apps/mobile/lib/features/broadcast/manager/broadcast_editor_manager.dart#L98) — it then calls `_active.enter(LiveEnterRequest(mode: .host))`.
3. [active_broadcast_manager.dart:127](apps/mobile/lib/features/broadcast/manager/active_broadcast_manager.dart#L127) — `LiveEnterMode.host` maps to **`_http.goLive` again**, with the same idempotency key.

The second call reaches `go_live`, the row is now `active`, and `existing.is_live()` returns 409 `ALREADY_LIVE`. So `_enter` fails, `entry.isEntered` is false, and the editor returns early without setting `step` — the row is **live on the server while the app is still on the form**. That is the exact shape the commented-out block at lines 112–150 documents as correct ("doing it here too would be a second go-live … and return 409 ALREADY_LIVE").

The idempotency key does *not* rescue it: the API's replay entry is written in a `tokio::spawn` ([idempotency.rs:420](apps/api/src/middleware/idempotency.rs#L420)), so the immediate second call usually misses the cache and runs the handler, or hits the in-flight claim.

Then every retry fails the same way, for a second reason:

4. `step.value = .started` is only recorded **after** entry succeeds ([line 108](apps/mobile/lib/features/broadcast/manager/broadcast_editor_manager.dart#L108)). The broadcast already committed at step 85, but the draft stays at `.created`. Pressing "Continue & Start" again re-enters `startBroadcast`, re-issues `/live`, and gets `ALREADY_LIVE` forever. Nothing navigates, so the button "does nothing".

## 2. Issue 2 — `status: active` + `state: ended`

The API can produce a row that is live to some queries and dead to others, and your database has one right now.

- `mark_live` ([repository/pg.rs:275](apps/api/src/modules/broadcast/repository/pg.rs#L275)) sets `status='active', published_at=$2` and **never clears `end_time`/`end_reason`**. Its only guard is `status='inactive'`.
- `find_live_by_creator` ([pg.rs:304](apps/api/src/modules/broadcast/repository/pg.rs#L304)) and `list_live` ([pg.rs:316](apps/api/src/modules/broadcast/repository/pg.rs#L316)) filter on `status='active'` alone — no `end_time IS NULL`.

So restart a broadcast that was already ended (exactly what happens when the draft from issue 1 still carries `createdBroadcastId`, or when you reopen it and press Continue), and you get `status='active'` with `end_time` set. `Broadcast::state()` derives from `end_time`, so:

| Consumer | Predicate | Result on that row |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /broadcasts?status=active` (Now Live) | status | **shows as live** |
| `state` field | `end_time` | **ended** |
| `POST /end` | `is_live()` = active **&&** no `end_time` | `NOT_LIVE` |
| `POST /resume` (app recovery) | `is_live()` | `NOT_LIVE` → recovery silently does nothing |
| `POST /broadcasts` (create) | `find_live_by_creator` | `ALREADY_LIVE_ELSEWHERE` |
| Reaper | `list_live` | sees it, but only after a 10-minute sweep |

That table is your whole report: it looks live on Home, Postman can't end it, and recovery can't resume it. This is audit finding **H18 / Step 56** almost verbatim ("start accepts a previously ended inactive row without clearing its ending fields, so an ended broadcast can become active while still reporting ended").

## 3. A third defect you almost certainly hit

`EndBroadcastDto` **requires `creatorName`** ([dtos.dart:154](apps/mobile/lib/features/broadcast/model/dtos.dart#L154)), but the API's `EndBroadcastResponse` does not send it. So when the app ends a broadcast, the server ends it and the client throws while parsing — the UI reports failure, and the manager records an unconfirmed outcome. That is audit **H05 / Step 51**, and it explains why ending via Postman became the workaround.

The same finding's other half is still open too: `removeCohost` sends `?remove_from_room=` as a **query parameter** and expects a `CohostDto`, while the API reads a JSON body `{removeFromRoom}` and answers with an envelope whose `data` is `null`.

import 'package:flutter/foundation.dart';

import 'package:meno_mobile/features/broadcast/services/_services.dart';
import 'package:uuid/uuid.dart';

/// The form that writes a broadcast, and the draft behind it.
///
/// Creating a broadcast is four steps the API has no single call for — create
/// the row, store its cover, go live for a token, hand the session to the live
/// owner — and the draft records how far it got, so a creation interrupted
/// between two of them is resumed rather than started again. A draft is written
/// on every edit for the
/// same reason: the form is the only place the user's work lives until the API
/// has it.
final class BroadcastEditorManager implements Disposable {
  new({
    required this._http,
    required this._local,
    required this._media,
    required this._active,
    required this._userId,
    required this._logger,
  }) {
    loadDrafts = .createSyncNoParamNoResult(
      _loadDrafts,
      errorFilterFn: menoExceptionFilter,
      debugName: 'broadcast.editor.loadDrafts',
    );

    createBroadcast = .createAsyncNoResult<BroadcastDraft>(
      (draft) async {
        if (_createdBroadcastId != null &&
            step.value.index >= BroadcastCreationStep.created.index) {
          // The row exists but its cover may not: an earlier press can have
          // stopped between the two, and going live now would leave the picture
          // the user picked on this device alone.
          await _uploadArtwork();
          return;
        }

        final created = await _http.create(
          // The draft's own key: a retry of this creation is the same logical
          // operation, so the API replays what it already did instead of making
          // a second broadcast (audit H20).
          idempotencyKey: draft.idempotencyKey.isEmpty
              ? (_createKey ??= _uuid.v4())
              : draft.idempotencyKey,
          title: draft.title,
          description: (draft.description?.isEmpty ?? false)
              ? null
              : draft.description,
          imageId: draft.imageId,
          cohosts: [for (final id in draft.cohosts) id.getOrCrash],
          recordingEnabled: draft.record,
        );
        _createdBroadcastId = created.id;
        step.value = .created;
        await _persistCreationState(created.id, step.value);

        // Before the chain goes on to `startBroadcast`: the cover is stored
        // under the broadcast's id, and the API refuses to change the cover of
        // a row that is already on air.
        await _uploadArtwork();
      },
      errorFilterFn: menoExceptionFilter,
      debugName: 'broadcast.editor.create',
    );

    startBroadcast = .createAsyncNoParamNoResult(
      () async {

The editor went live **twice** per press: `startBroadcast` called `POST /broadcasts/{id}/live` itself, then asked `ActiveBroadcastManager.enter(LiveEnterMode.host)` to do it again. The second call hit the "already on air" guard, so the entry never opened a room — and because `step` was only recorded *after* a successful entry, the draft stayed at `created` and every retry repeated the same double go-live. The row was live on the server while the app sat on the form.

Mobile changes:

- [broadcast_editor_manager.dart](apps/mobile/lib/features/broadcast/manager/broadcast_editor_manager.dart) — `_goLive` is now the single go-live, it records `.started` **at the commit** (before entry), and treats `ALREADY_LIVE` as the commit it is instead of an error. When the broadcast already exists, entry re-mints via `resume` rather than asking for a second `/live`. A retry therefore always has a forward path, and the label ladder (`Start Broadcast` → `Continue & Start` → `Finalize Broadcast`) now matches reality.
- [active_broadcast_manager.dart](apps/mobile/lib/features/broadcast/manager/active_broadcast_manager.dart) — `LiveEnterRequest.session` lets the caller attach a session it already paid for, so `enter` is purely local when the token is in hand.
- `_forgetStartedDraft` deletes the draft once the room is entered, and `_resetCreationState` clears `_createdBroadcastId` unconditionally — a finished draft can no longer point the next creation at a terminal row.
- `_uploadArtwork` now skips past `.started`: the API refuses a cover change on a live row, so a resumed draft keeps the artwork it has instead of failing the chain it was meant to finish.
- The page only navigates when `session.value` exists, which is now only true after a real entry.

## Issue 2 — `status: active` with `state: ended`

These are two different fields and the API let them disagree. `status` is the row's lifecycle (`inactive`/`active`); `state` is derived — live **iff** `end_time` is null. `mark_live` set `status='active'` without looking at `end_time`, and `find_live_by_creator`/`list_live` filtered on `status` alone. So re-opening an ended row produced a broadcast the catalogue called live, that `end` refused as not live (`BROADCAST NOT LIVE` in Postman), that `resume`/`token` refused, and that permanently occupied the creator's one on-air slot.

API changes (all in `6c8310f`):

- [pg.rs](apps/api/src/modules/broadcast/repository/pg.rs) — `mark_live` requires `end_time IS NULL AND end_reason IS NULL`; `find_live_by_creator` and `list_live` filter on `end_time IS NULL`, mirroring `Broadcast::is_live()`. [memory.rs](apps/api/src/modules/broadcast/repository/memory.rs) mirrors it for service tests.
- [service.rs](apps/api/src/modules/broadcast/service.rs) — `end` is idempotent: a row that already has an end returns its summary instead of 409, so a lost response or a stuck row can always be closed. The media token is minted before the row commits, so a mint failure leaves nothing live.
- [0018_broadcast_ended_row_repair.sql](crates/db/migrations/0018_broadcast_ended_row_repair.sql) — repairs existing `active` + `end_time` rows to `inactive`, then adds `broadcasts_live_has_no_end_check` so no future writer can recreate the shape.
- New error code in [error.rs](crates/core/src/error.rs) / [broadcast/error.rs](apps/api/src/modules/broadcast/error.rs).

**Run `sqlx migrate run` before testing** — your current stuck row is only fixed by that migration, not by the code alone.

Also included, from the H05 audit items: `EndBroadcastDto.creatorName` is defaulted (it is not in the payload, so every successful end used to fail to parse — that is the "server ended it while the app showed an error" symptom), and `removeCohost` sends `removeFromRoom` as a required JSON body while parsing no response.

## Test you asked me to drop

`broadcast_local_service_test.dart` depended on the ObjectBox native library, which isn't installed here, so its three draft-isolation cases failed before any of my code ran. I removed that group and moved the profile half, which passes and needs no FFI, to [profile_cache_isolation_test.dart](apps/mobile/test/features/profile/profile_cache_isolation_test.dart). Draft isolation is now untested until ObjectBox is available — worth restoring then.

## Verification run

- `cargo test -p meno-api --test broadcast_service` → 45 passed, including new cases for ending an ended row, refusing a terminal row in `mark_live`, and the idempotent end; `--test broadcast_router` passed. No API file has changed since.
- `flutter analyze` → **No issues found** (the long lines I introduced are wrapped).
- `flutter test test/features/broadcast` → **97 passed, 1 skipped**. The skip is the editor page widget test, already skipped upstream for the same ObjectBox reason.
- `flutter test test/features/profile/profile_cache_isolation_test.dart` → passed.
- Not verified: a real device run of create → kill → resume → end → Home, since that needs the API, Postgres migrations and a LiveKit room. The retry matrix is reasoned and covered by the API tests, but there is no mobile-level test for it — the manager needs ObjectBox to construct.

One thing still open from the audit list, unrelated to these two bugs: WS `endBroadcast`/`leaveBroadcast` and disconnect cleanup are still missing, so server-side participant counts drift on an unclean disconnect.

=== rules of the road
## 5. Rules of the road

### 5.1 Simplicity rules

Read these before writing a single class. They are how the guide stays followable.

1. **Concrete classes, constructor injection.** Every new manager/service takes its collaborators as constructor parameters. No `di<X>()` inside a method body outside `locator.dart`, the app composition files, and small view-composition boundaries (design §4.4).
2. **No interface per class.** An interface exists only where there is a real second implementation today: `RoomTransport` (LiveKit vs silent fake) and `TokenBlocklist` (already exists on the backend). Everything else gets a concrete fake in `test/_support/`.
3. **No event bus, no generic framework, no new DI tier.** Commands are for user actions; plain `Future` methods are for internal sequencing (audit §4).
4. **Prefer fewer files.** One file may hold two or three tightly related small types (`AccountContext` + `RequestIdentity`; `CredentialRecord` + `VaultEnvelope` + `RememberedIdentity`). Never a file per field.
5. **Immutable data, mutable owners.** Models are `final` + freezed. Managers own their mutable state (`ValueNotifier`); nothing else writes it.
6. **One writer per fact.** Credentials: `SessionStore`. Account selection: `AccountTransitionOwner`. Live phase: `ActiveBroadcastManager`. Current-profile presentation: `MyProfileManager`. A second writer is a bug.
7. **Fence after every await.** Any `await` in account-scoped code is followed by a check that the generation/epoch/owner is still live before the next side effect. This is the single most important habit in the guide.
8. **Dispose everything you create**, in reverse creation order, idempotently. `finally` closes resources; server outcomes never gate local cleanup.
9. **No `BuildContext` across an await.** Capture what you need before the gap.
10. **Enums for payload-free sets, native sealed classes for outcomes that carry data.** `LivePhase`, `AccountPhase`, `RenewalState` are enums. `RefreshOutcome`, `TransitionResult`, `MutationResult` are native Dart 3 sealed classes with exhaustive `switch`. No code generation for either. No booleans standing in for three-way states.

### 5.2 Freezed policy

| Use                                                   | What                                                                                             | Why (one line each)                                                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Freezed**                                           | `CredentialRecord`, `LiveSnapshot`, `AccountSnapshot`                                            | The only places where `copyWith` earns its place. Value equality is what makes `select` comparisons trustworthy.                                                         |
| **Hand-written `final class`** with `==` / `hashCode` | `AccountContext`, `RequestIdentity`, `VaultEnvelope`, `RememberedIdentity`, `PendingDestination` | Small immutable values. A few lines of equality code is cheaper than a generated file.                                                                                   |
| **`enum`**                                            | `AccountPhase`, `LivePhase`, `RenewalState`, `LoginFormMode`                                     | Payload-free closed sets. Exhaustive `switch` works without codegen.                                                                                                     |
| **Native `sealed class`**                             | `RefreshOutcome`, `TransitionResult`, `MutationResult`                                           | Outcomes that carry data: the compiler forces every caller to handle rejection, uncertainty and cancellation.                                                            |
| **No**                                                | Services, managers, notifiers, widgets, anything with a lifecycle                                | Value-class generators have no `dispose` and hide ownership.                                                                                                             |
| **No** (hand-written decode)                          | Vault/secrets storage shapes                                                                     | Storage must _fail closed_: a missing or malformed field returns `null`/typed failure. Blind generated decoding throws deep inside the class instead of at the boundary. |

How to combine freezed with fail-closed decoding (Step 2 does exactly this):

- The class declares the shape (freezed for `CredentialRecord`; hand-written `final class` for `VaultEnvelope` and `RememberedIdentity`).
- A hand-written `static CredentialRecord? tryDecode(Map<String, dynamic>? json)` performs **every** field check itself and returns `null` on the first violation, constructing the value only after all checks pass.
- Generated `fromJson` is not used for these types; serialization is a hand-written `Map<String, dynamic> toJson()` on the same class.

### 5.3 Naming and folder conventions

| Kind                                      | Where it goes                                                                                                                                           | Example                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| Immutable model / union                   | `lib/features/<feature>/model/` (or `lib/_routing/` for routing values)                                                                                 | `features/auth/model/account_context.dart`                 |
| Service (one external boundary)           | `lib/features/<feature>/services/`; only genuinely cross-feature services stay in `lib/_shared/services/`                                               | `features/auth/services/session_store.dart`                |
| Manager (semantic business logic)         | `lib/features/<feature>/manager/`                                                                                                                       | `features/broadcast/manager/active_broadcast_manager.dart` |
| App composition and lifecycle owners      | `lib/app/`                                                                                                                                              | `app/account_transition_owner.dart`                        |
| Widget                                    | `features/<feature>/pages/` (full screen) or `widgets/` (part of a screen)                                                                              | `features/profile/pages/user_profile_page.dart`            |
| Reusable widget with no feature knowledge | `lib/_shared/widgets/`                                                                                                                                  | `_shared/widgets/feed_widget.dart`                         |
| Test                                      | mirror the `lib` path under `test/`                                                                                                                     | `test/features/auth/session_store_test.dart`               |
| Test fake / clock                         | `test/_support/`                                                                                                                                        | `test/_support/fake_secure_storage.dart`                   |
| Rust module                               | `apps/api/src/modules/<module>/`: wire types in `dto.rs`, SQL in `repository/pg.rs`, rules in `service.rs`, HTTP in `handlers.rs`, WS in `routes/ws.rs` | `apps/api/src/modules/broadcast/service.rs`                |
| Rust test                                 | `apps/api/tests/<area>_<layer>.rs`                                                                                                                      | `apps/api/tests/broadcast_service.rs`                      |

Naming rules: class names say what they own (`AccountTransitionOwner`, not `AccountHelper`); no `Impl` suffix unless a real interface exists; no `_v2` suffix on classes — versions live in storage keys and schema fields.

`lib/app` → `features` → `_shared` → `_core`. Never the reverse. `_shared` must not import `features` or `app` (audit M22). Feature-to-feature calls go through a small public file in that feature, never a broad barrel.

Verified against the guide's Phase B (Steps 51, 52, 56, 57, 58), its Rules of the road (§5.1–5.4), and the audit finding each step implements. One genuine deviation turned up, and I fixed it; the rest is aligned or explicitly incomplete rather than off-course.

## The deviation I found and fixed

**Step 51** is explicit on two things my earlier mobile change got half-right. It says the end DTO must mirror the payload *exactly* — "NO `creatorName`: it is not in the payload" — and Step 52 adds "DO NOT add `creatorName` … that would create a second source for display identity (M12)". I had kept the field and defaulted it to `''`, which is exactly the tolerated-drift shape the step warns about: a renamed or dropped server field would pass silently, and the ended screen gets a blank name rather than the local fallback.

Fixed in [dtos.dart](apps/mobile/lib/features/broadcast/model/dtos.dart): `creatorName` is gone from `EndBroadcastDto`, `toDomain` no longer reads it (the domain `EndedBroadcast` keeps its own empty default, to be enriched from the profile source if a surface ever shows it), and `endedAt` is now `required` with `parseRfc3339`, matching the Rust field's non-optional `ended_at`. The test that injected `'creatorName': 'Ada Lovelace'` into a payload the server never sends now asserts the real shape and the empty fallback in [broadcast_dto_test.dart](apps/mobile/test/features/broadcast/broadcast_dto_test.dart).

The other half of Step 51 — `removeCohost` returning `Future<void>`, sending `removeFromRoom` in a **required** JSON body, parsing no response — was already correct, and `remove_cohost` in [handlers.rs](apps/api/src/modules/broadcast/handlers.rs) already answers `204`/no content.

## Where the change matches the guide

**Step 56 (backend retry safety)** — `go_live` now refuses terminal rows before any write (`end_time` **or** `status == ended`), creates the room and mints the token *before* the commit, and commits through a conditional `UPDATE` that also requires `end_time IS NULL AND end_reason IS NULL`, so "error" means "did not happen". A booking that loses the race re-reads and answers `BROADCAST_ALREADY_ENDED` instead of blaming `ALREADY_LIVE`. Ending fields are never cleared — the guide forbids it in those words. No row deletion or compensating write was introduced, matching the step's watch-out.

**Step 57 (editor honesty)** — the behavioural core is the guide's: `started` now means the *server* committed, is recorded at the commit, and retry resumes at the incomplete phase rather than at zero; a local entry failure leaves `started` and retries only the entry; navigation happens only after a real entry (`session.value` is set solely on an entered result), which is precisely "never treat `started` as `entered`".

**Step 58 (logical keys, mobile half)** — one key per logical start (`_liveKey ??= uuid`), reused on every retry, cleared only when the form moves to a new broadcast; the draft's own key is persisted and forwarded for create; `join`/`end` already accepted keys. No key is generated inside a retry loop or interceptor.

**Rules of the road** — no new dependency, no interface, no DI tier, no event bus (§5.1 1–3); the live phase still has one writer, `ActiveBroadcastManager` (§5.1 6); the manager still fences every entry against `_exiting`/generation, and my only change inside it replaced one await with `request.session ?? await …` without moving that fence (§5.1 7); new types are enums/`final class`/freezed-tests per §5.2; naming and file placement follow §5.3; the new `BROADCAST_ALREADY_ENDED` code is mirrored in [error.rs](crates/core/src/error.rs) and [meno_exception.dart](apps/mobile/lib/_core/exceptions/meno_exception.dart) in the 409 group, per the repo's add-never-rename contract.

## What is genuinely not done (gaps, not veers)

- **Step 57 is partially implemented.** The prescribed phase enum (`.creating/.uploading/.uploaded/.starting/.entering/.entered`) does not exist — `BroadcastCreationStep` is still `{none, created, started, saved}` — so no phase is shown, fields are not edit-locked during a run, `isRunning` still covers only the start command, and H19's "patch edits made before a retry" is absent. Create/upload/start remain two chained commands rather than the single `publish()` operation.
- **Step 52 is untouched.** No `broadcasts-end` fixture, no `apps/api/tests/broadcast_contract.rs`, no doc line on `EndBroadcastResponse`. So the guide's "both sides assert the same fixture" guarantee is missing, and Step 51's `broadcast_contract_test.dart` cannot exist yet.
- **H05's server-side default survives.** `remove_cohost` still reads `Option<Json<RemoveCohostRequest>>` with `unwrap_or(true)`, so a caller that omits the body still gets eviction — the exact "keep listening defaults to eviction" hazard, now only prevented by the client. Step 52's wording ("read body `RemoveCohostRequest`") argues for making it required.
- **Step 56's atomicity bullet is only half met.** The creator's participant row is still inserted by a separate `join` call *after* `mark_live`, not in the same transaction; a failure between them leaves a live row with no host presence.

/// The live session this device is in the middle of, kept for the next start.
///
/// A broadcast outlives the app process. A phone that is killed mid-session
/// leaves a room on the server that still lists this client, and — for a host —
/// a broadcast still on air with nobody publishing into it. What is written
/// here says *which* broadcast and *whose* session that was, nothing more: a
/// media token is never persisted (M18). Recovery always asks the API for a
/// fresh one — [`BroadcastHttpService.resume`] is the endpoint that answers
/// "I am still the host (or a listener) of this room" — so a record here always
/// means "this was still running when the process stopped" and never carries a
/// credential across a restart.
///
/// It belongs to one account: a room is entered with a session minted for one
/// identity, and re-entering it as another would join under the wrong name.
/// [read] therefore also requires the stored owner to be this store's owner —
/// a record for anyone else reads as none, never as something to resume.
final class LiveSessionStore {
  /// Creates a store over [_storage] for the account [_userId] names.
  const new(this._storage, {required this._userId});

  /// The record's shape version; a record written by another version is
  /// unreadable rather than half-read.
  static const int _version = 1;

  final LocalStorage _storage;
  final Id _userId;

  /// The session this account was in, or null when it ended cleanly — or when
  /// the record belongs to another account or cannot be read.
  SavedLiveSession? read() {
    final json = _storage.getString(_key);
    if (json == null) return null;

    try {
      final record = jsonDecode(json) as Map<String, dynamic>;
      if (record['version'] != _version) return null;
      if (record['ownerId'] != _userId.getOrCrash) return null;

      final broadcastId = Id.fromString(record['broadcastId'] as String);
      if (!broadcastId.isValid) return null;

      return SavedLiveSession(
        broadcastId: broadcastId,
        roleHint: record['roleHint'] as String?,
        savedAt: DateTime.parse(record['savedAt'] as String),
      );
    } on Object {
      return null;
    }
  }

  /// Remembers [session] until it ends.
  ///
  /// Only the identity of the session is stored: who owns it, which broadcast,
  /// which side of the room it was on, and when. The token the API minted is
  /// deliberately dropped — it is short-lived anyway, and preferences are not
  /// where a bearer token belongs.
  Future<void> save(BroadcastSession session) {
    return _storage.setString(
      _key,
      value: jsonEncode({
        'version': _version,
        'ownerId': _userId.getOrCrash,
        'broadcastId': session.broadcast.id.getOrCrash,
        'roleHint': session.broadcast.hostId == _userId
            ? _hostRole
            : _listenerRole,
        'savedAt': DateTime.now().toUtc().toIso8601String(),
      }),
    );
  }

  /// Forgets the session.
  Future<void> clear() => _storage.remove(_key);

        &self,
        id: Uuid,
        actor: &UserSummary,

        let existing = self.require(id).await?;
        if !existing.is_live() {
            return Err(error::not_live());

            connections = MAX_WS_CONNECTIONS_PER_USER,

        return Err(Failure(MenoError::RateLimited {
            retry_after_secs: ttl::RECONNECT_RATE.as_secs(),

All three traced, and two of them share a single root cause.

## Issue 1 — the socket's 401

Your dev socket URL had no path. `.env.dev` had `WEB_SOCKET_URL=ws://localhost:8080`, so the client handshook against `/` instead of `/ws`. I confirmed this against the running API:

| request | status | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /` | **401** | exactly what your client logged |
| `GET /ws` | 400 | the route exists, and it is asking for a token |
| `GET /ws?token=bogus` | 400 | parsed and rejected at the gate |

It also rules out "no token": `SocketClient._connect` refuses to connect at all when the credential supplier returns null, so a token was sent — to the wrong path.

Fixed:
- `apps/mobile/.env.dev` → `WEB_SOCKET_URL=ws://localhost:8080/ws` (this file is gitignored, so it is your machine only).
- [.env.example](apps/mobile/.env.example) now documents the requirement, so the next checkout does not repeat it.
- `env.g.dart` regenerated. Note that Envied served a **stale cached value** here: a normal `build_runner build` reported `0 outputs`, and even deleting `env.g.dart` only rebuilt it with the old URL. It needed `rm -rf .dart_tool/build` first. I verified the generated constant is now `ws://localhost:8080/ws` with a throwaway test (the value is obfuscated in the generated file, so reading it directly proves nothing).

**You need a full stop and `flutter run`** — `@Envied` compiles the value into the app, so a hot restart may keep the old kernel.

## Issue 2 — recovery after restart did nothing

The mechanism is intact: `ActiveBroadcastManager._enter` writes the recovery record with `_store.save(details)` after a successful entry, and `recover()` runs at account-scope registration, reading that record and calling `/resume`. It is strictly record-driven.

The record was never written in your run, because entry failed on the `runAsync` assertion right after the join — the save only happens after `_publishLive`, which the failure skipped. So there was nothing for `recover()` to find, even though the broadcast was live on the server. With the `attach()` fix, entry completes, the record is written, and a restart mid-session will resume.

Worth knowing, and left as-is deliberately:
- A broadcast that is committed on the server but was never entered locally (or whose record is lost) will **not** auto-recover. `recover()` never asks the server "do I own a live broadcast?".
- The manual path exists: the **Now Live** card on Home opens the pre-stream modal, which resumes that broadcast.
- `onReconnected` is exposed by `BroadcastSocketService` but nothing consumes it, so events missed while the socket is down are not reconciled on reconnect. That is a separate gap.

## Issue 3 — ending from Postman notifies nobody

The backend does what you expect, and the client is wired for it — nothing was arriving because the socket was never connected.

- [service.rs](apps/api/src/modules/broadcast/service.rs) emits `ended(row.id, EndReason::Normal, &recipients)` where recipients are the creator, current cohosts **and** the users LiveKit reports present — then calls `notify_home()`, a global `homeInvalidated` nudge.
- [broadcast_socket_service.dart](apps/mobile/lib/features/broadcast/services/broadcast_socket_service.dart) registers handlers for both `endedBroadcast` and `homeInvalidated`.
- [broadcast_feed_data_source.dart](apps/mobile/lib/features/broadcast/manager/broadcast_feed_data_source.dart) refreshes the feed on `homeInvalidated` and on `endedBroadcast`, and `ActiveBroadcastManager` subscribes to `onEndedBroadcast`, so the room moves to ended.

So after the URL fix, ending from Postman should push to every connected device and drop the broadcast from Home. Two limits to be aware of: a viewer who is neither the creator, a cohost, nor present in LiveKit will not receive the *targeted* ended event (they get the global home nudge on their next refresh), and a device whose socket is disconnected at that moment learns nothing until it reconnects or refetches.

//! Broadcast chat: a message history, reactions, and the socket events that carry them.
//!
//! # What this module is
//!
//! The conversation inside a live broadcast. A participant sends a message or a
//! reaction over the socket they are already holding; everybody in the room hears
//! about it on the same socket; and the history is readable over one HTTP endpoint so a
//! client that just joined does not have to replay the room to see what was said.
//!
//! # Parts
//!
//! | File | Answers |
//! | --- | --- |
//! | [`model`] | what a message and a reaction *are*, and the edit window that governs them |
//! | [`dto`] | what the wire carries (camelCase, RFC 3339 — §9.5) |
//! | [`error`] | which taxonomy entry a refusal is (§4.2) |
//! | [`repository`] | what is stored — Postgres ([`repository::pg`]) and the §10 double ([`repository::memory`]) |
//! | [`publisher`] | how a stored event reaches a room's sockets (§3.1) |
//! | [`service`] | the rules, in order |
//! | [`handlers`] | the one HTTP read; the writes arrive on the socket ([`crate::routes::ws`]) |
//! | [`state`] | which adapters those trait objects are bound to (§5.6) |
//!
//! # What changed from `master`, and why
//!
//! `master`'s chat module is the one this replaces
//! (`apps/api/src/modules/chat/`, and `apps/api/src/routes/chat.rs`). Four changes are
//! structural rather than cosmetic, and each is a bug the old shape made possible:
//!

//!    `is_active_broadcast`, then `is_broadcast_participant`, then inserted. Between
//!    the second answer and the insert a broadcast could end or a participant be
//!    removed, and the message landed anyway — a row in a room nobody is in.

///
/// `data` is left as raw JSON: the concrete shape depends on `event`, and the read
/// loop deserialises it into the matching request type once the event is known.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
pub struct ClientMessage {
    /// Which client action this is.
    pub event: WsEvent,
    /// The action's arguments.
    pub data: Value,
}

pub struct WsQuery {

/// The one read a chat has.
///
/// Everything that writes chat arrives on the socket — `apps/api/src/routes/chat.rs`
/// serves exactly `GET /broadcasts/{id}/chat/messages` and nothing else — so a
/// feed depends on a page reader, not on a client, and a test can answer pages
/// without a transport.
abstract interface class ChatMessagePageReader {
  /// Reads one page of [broadcastId]'s chat history, newest first.
  ///
  /// [cursor] is the opaque cursor the previous page handed back, or null to ask
  /// for the first page.
  Future<CursorPage<Message>> messages(
    Id broadcastId, {
    String? cursor,
    int limit,
    CancelToken? cancelToken,
  });
}

/// The chat module's HTTP surface.
///
/// The endpoint refuses a caller who is not in the room (`403 NOT_PARTICIPANT`)
/// and answers with the API's cursor envelope:
///
/// ```json
/// { "data": [...], "next_cursor": "opaque", "has_next_page": true }
/// ```
///
/// The cursor is stored and handed back untouched — this client never builds one.
final class ChatHttpService implements ChatMessagePageReader {
  const new(this._client);

  final HttpClient _client;

  /// How many messages one page holds when the caller does not say.
  static const int defaultPageSize = 50;

  @override
  Future<CursorPage<Message>> messages(
    Id broadcastId, {
    String? cursor,
    int limit = defaultPageSize,
    CancelToken? cancelToken,
  }) {
    return _client.get(
      '/broadcasts/${broadcastId.getOrCrash}/chat/messages',
      queryParameters: {'cursor': ?cursor, 'limit': limit},
      cancelToken: cancelToken,
      fromJson: (data) => CursorPage.fromJson(
        data,
        (item) => MessageDto.fromJson(item).toDomain,
        logger: _client.logger,
      ),
    );
  }
}

/// The one proxy per message id, and how many holders each has.
///
/// Two lists may show the same message — the feed and a sheet opened from it —
/// and both must see an edit. Keeping one proxy per id is what makes that
/// possible without the second list refetching, and reference counting is what
/// decides when it can be thrown away.
final class ChatDataRepository implements Disposable {
  final _proxies = <String, MessageProxy>{};

  /// The proxy for [message]'s id, refreshed with [message]'s body.
  ///
  /// A known id keeps its proxy — and so keeps every row already drawing it —
  /// while taking the new body. The caller owes a [release] for this reference.
  MessageProxy acquire(Message message) {
    final key = message.id.getOrCrash();
    final existing = _proxies[key];
    if (existing != null) {
      existing.target = message;
      existing.referenceCount++;
      return existing;
    }

    final proxy = MessageProxy(message)..referenceCount = 1;
    _proxies[key] = proxy;
    return proxy;
  }

  /// Gives one reference back, disposing the proxy when it was the last.
  void release(MessageProxy proxy) {
    proxy.referenceCount--;
    if (proxy.referenceCount > 0) return;
    _proxies.remove(proxy.idStr);
    proxy.dispose();
  }

  /// Gives back one reference per proxy in [proxies].
  void releaseAll(Iterable<MessageProxy> proxies) {
    for (final proxy in List<MessageProxy>.of(proxies)) {
      release(proxy);
    }
  }

  @override
  FutureOr<dynamic> onDispose() async {
    for (final proxy in _proxies.values) {
      proxy.dispose();
    }
    _proxies.clear();
  }
}
